title: Add a Grok usage collector for the agents panel
head: 72221e9aef84
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: An expired-token check can consume and discard Grok's rotating refresh token
leads.consequence: If the IdP returns a replacement refresh_token, the collector keeps only access_token in memory. Grok's auth.json retains the now-spent refresh token, so subsequent CLI refreshes may get invalid_grant and force another interactive sign-in; subsequent collector runs can no longer refresh either. Reuse Grok's credential manager or avoid refreshing externally; do not rotate without saving both tokens under the CLI's auth lock.

leads.summary: The CLI's credits-config Build product enum is ignored by the promised limits row
leads.consequence: The credits-config shape tested by the official CLI, with product=PRODUCT_GROK_BUILD and usagePercent=57, produces only the weekly total, not the Grok Build meter promised by the README/manual. Match the actual enum and cover it with a producer-derived fixture.
leads.triage: matches Opus Q-A; published as open question (fixture only, CLI does not read productUsage yet)

leads.summary: Cache-creation input is counted twice in local token totals
leads.consequence: Grok's inputTokens includes both cached-read and cache-creation input. A row input=100, cachedRead=60, cacheCreation=20, output=5 should total 105, but the collector emits buckets (40,5,60,20) totalling 125. Today, recent-days, all-time model totals and synced usage overstate tokens, while the existing test mistakenly expects this split. Subtract both cache buckets from fresh input.

leads.summary: Forked sessions and folded subagent usage are billed again in the directory-wide walk
leads.consequence: Grok copies usage.json including previously billed turns when forking and assigns the child a new sessionId. The collector adds every matched usage file without deduplicating inherited turns, so one turn in a parent and full fork becomes two prompts and double tokens, amplified by further forks. Subagent usage also folds into the parent's ledger, yet the child's session is separately persisted under sessions. Exclude already attributed/copy-prefix usage using session metadata, or derive prompt events from non-inherited records.

leads.summary: Weekly limit cache crosses Grok homes and accounts
leads.consequence: The limits cache is always one grok-limits.json under XDG_CACHE_HOME and stores neither user_id nor GROK_HOME. Switching accounts/homes, signing out, or having a short outage serves a prior account's weekly percentage as the current user's; for the first 15 seconds a newly signed-in user is served the old figure without even probing. Key/validate the cache by auth identity and home before fallback/reuse.
leads.triage: verified factual but matches existing claude-limits.json precedent (claude collector line 800); low value; not published

leads.summary: Sub-one-percent billing values render as 100 times the real percentage
leads.consequence: The backend percentage is 0 to 100. If overall creditUsagePercent is 0.5 and no product row is >=1, the collector assumes fractional scale and emits 0.5, which the panel shows as 50%, rather than 0.005 / 0.5%. The affected user starts every new period with a materially inflated meter. Normalize the known percentage units unconditionally.

The official CLI reads an overridden credential path via GROK_AUTH_PATH, including users with a separate credential file or custom identity provider. The collector reads only GROK_HOME/auth.json, so such a user sees Waiting for auth or an unrelated account's limits while the CLI is signed in. Resolve the same auth path as Grok.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus F1 sub-point; published

leads.summary: Missing expires_at means the collector never refreshes a token Grok considers expired
leads.consequence: Grok supports OAuth credentials with no expires_at; it derives an expiry from create_time plus 30 days. This collector treats absent expires_at as zero and zero as not expired, sends an old bearer to billing repeatedly, and never attempts refresh even if refresh_token is present. A 401 becomes 'Grok limits unavailable' while Grok itself can refresh. Use Grok's fallback validity rule or avoid managing the CLI's tokens.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus F1 sub-point; published

leads.summary: Legacy monthlyLimit/used billing response yields no limits at all
leads.consequence: The CLI's supported legacy response may contain monthlyLimit.val and used.val plus billingPeriodStart/End without creditUsagePercent. The collector derives the period title but returns [] without calculating used/monthlyLimit, so an account with no local sessions has no tab despite an available monthly meter; with sessions the limits section disappears. Test with a legacy-only payload and derive the percentage.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator (full.diff limits test legacy case has creditUsagePercent 25; Opus billing_parse legacy_shape_no_percent = []); folded into F3; published

leads.summary: Three other open Grok collectors collide with this new command and manifest
leads.consequence: Open PRs #12352, #6485 and #10400 each independently add bin/omarchy-agent-usage-grok and grok provider/assets. Their heads diverge from this PR and a three-way merge with absent base file has conflict markers in the collector for each; these are competing implementations, not additive providers. Maintainers must select/consolidate one rather than merge both as separate changes. Each PR is reported MERGEABLE against its own target, not against this head; merged-code tests cannot run while conflicts remain unresolved.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus related-PR analysis; published

leads.summary: Usage caches are forcibly world-readable even though the sibling collectors are moving to owner-only
leads.consequence: write_json chmods both model/day usage and limits caches to 0644. Where a user's cache root and parents are traversable (for example a configured shared XDG_CACHE_HOME), other local users can read private usage/model/day data; mkstemp's default 0600 would avoid this. New tests assert 0644, whereas open #12265 tightens Claude/Codex caches to owner-only. Preserve 0600 and adjust mode tests.
leads.triage: matches existing Claude/Codex collectors (chmod 0o644); mentioned only as consistency note with #12265

leads.summary: Missing reset timestamps keep old credit limits indefinitely during an outage
leads.consequence: The CLI's credits period fields are optional. A successfully fetched percentage with neither currentPeriod.end nor billingPeriodEnd is cached with resetsAt='', and limit_window_open declares the entry live forever. During offline/expired-token conditions the old percentage remains displayed indefinitely rather than expiring by age or being marked last known. Bound the cache's age when there is no reset deadline.
leads.triage: edge case (requires payload without any period end); not published

leads.summary: Grok Build fixture uses an invented product enum and masks the missing row
leads.consequence: The fixture passes when the collector only recognizes GrokBuild and would fail to catch the official CLI's credits-config fixture product=PRODUCT_GROK_BUILD. Change the fixture to the actual credits-config product and assert two rows; this is a targeted test fidelity defect in addition to H02.

leads.summary: Tier label relies solely on undocumented access-token claims
leads.consequence: The CLI obtains the subscription label from remote settings or /user?include=subscription rather than a documented JWT tier mapping. If issued access tokens omit tier/plan/subscription_tier (the public token parser does not require those claims), the billing call succeeds but the panel's hero says only 'Subscription'. Confirm with an actual redacted issued-token claim set or use the CLI's account metadata instead.
leads.triage: unconfirmed by hunter; Opus found JWT tier numbering matches Grok jwt_tier_claim; dropped

leads.summary: Choosing the first auth.json value can select a legacy login instead of the active Grok OAuth scope
leads.consequence: Grok stores credentials in a sorted scope-to-credential map, not an unordered list of equivalent accounts. With a retained https://accounts.x.ai/sign-in legacy entry and the current https://auth.x.ai::client_id entry, the collector selects the first valid legacy bearer and sends it to the xAI-only billing endpoint even though Grok itself selects the active OIDC scope and deliberately ignores legacy WebLogin tokens. The panel can report unavailable or stale/wrong-account limits despite a signed-in CLI, depending on how the proxy handles the legacy token. Choose the CLI's active configured OAuth scope and reject non-xAI/legacy entries.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus F1 sub-point (entry_selection probe); published

limits: No calls to the actual xAI endpoints or real credentials. Claims about the live billing producer use the public xai-org/grok-build source at f0e3be11 (its xai-grok-version/Cargo.toml:4 says 1.0.41) and its credits-config fixture, not a captured production HTTP response. The exact issued access-token claim set in H14 cannot be settled from published code alone.
No graphical shell was launched, QML consumer behavior was traced from source, not live-rendered.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the local-stats collector fits the agents panel contract. `omarchy-agent-usage-update` discovers it and writes `grok.json` with the same key set as the Claude record, and both new tests plus the existing agent-usage tests pass at head. The limits path has one significant issue: on an expired sign-in it redeems the Grok CLI's refresh token and discards the rotated replacement. There are also counting and parsing errors that inflate the numbers. Three other open PRs add the same collector file (see the end).

Grok CLI references below are to its public source, [xai-org/grok-build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) at `f0e3be1`, whose version crate reads `1.0.41` (the version the collector sends).

### Expired sign-in: the collector redeems the CLI's refresh token and discards the replacement

When the saved access token has expired (`bin/omarchy-agent-usage-grok:656`), `refresh_access_token` (line 460) POSTs the stored `refresh_token` to `auth.x.ai/oauth2/token`. It keeps only the new `access_token` and never writes `auth.json`. This happens before the 15-second reuse check (line 676), so every run while the token is expired makes a token request.

Synthetic probe (fake IdP that rotates refresh tokens and rejects reuse, no real endpoint contacted):

```text
run 1  presents rt-original -> receives rt-rotated -> billing OK, limits shown
       auth.json afterwards: byte-identical, still rt-original
run 2  presents rt-original -> invalid_grant -> "Sign-in expired"
run 3  presents rt-original -> invalid_grant -> "Sign-in expired"

4 consecutive --limits-only runs: 4 token requests, 1 billing request
```

Grok's source treats these tokens as single-use:
- `xai-grok-login/src/storage.rs:23`: "a refresh token can be used only once".
- `oidc/refresh.rs:29-35`: Grok assumes, as a "conservative client-side bound", that an IdP accepts an already-rotated token for about 60 s, and says re-sending it after that "trips the IdP's reuse detection and revokes a successor".
- On `invalid_grant` the CLI discards its stored tokens and asks the user to run `grok login`.

**Impact:** a user who leaves Grok closed past one access-token lifetime can find the Grok CLI signed out after the collector's next run. It then keeps re-presenting a spent token on every refresh and panel open. The collector is enabled by default. This consequence is inferred from Grok's source; the live IdP was not tested, and the token lifetime is not in source.

Smaller problems on the same path:
- `oauth_login` (line 418) picks the first `auth.json` entry with a `key` that has not expired (or has no expiry), regardless of scope or `auth_mode`. For example, when an expired OAuth entry comes first, a following API-key entry or legacy web-login entry is sent as the Bearer token to the billing endpoint.
- The token endpoint is hard-coded, so an enterprise OIDC entry's refresh token goes to `auth.x.ai`.
- An entry without `expires_at` is never treated as expired. The CLI applies a 30-day TTL from `create_time`.
- `GROK_AUTH_PATH`, which the CLI honours, is ignored.

**Suggested change:** drop `refresh_access_token` and follow `omarchy-agent-usage-claude` (lines 804-821), which deliberately does not refresh: report "Sign-in expired", serve open cached windows and let the Grok CLI refresh its own token. Alternatively, fetch billing through the CLI's ACP `_x.ai/billing` method, as #6485 and #10400 do. Select the entry by the xAI OAuth scope and skip `api_key` and `web_login` entries. No test covers the refresh path: a mutant with the refresh disabled passes both PR tests.

### Forked and subagent sessions are counted twice

`scan_sessions` sums every `sessions/**/usage.json` (line 272) without de-duplication.
- **Forks:** Grok copies the parent's `usage.json` turns into the fork with their original `endedAt` (`xai-grok-shell/src/session/storage/jsonl/copy.rs:384-402`, `copy_usage` defaults to true).
- **Subagents:** the parent's usage folds in each subagent's spend (`xai-chat-state/src/usage.rs:132-157`), and the child is a separate session directory marked `session_kind: "subagent"` in `summary.json`.

| Synthetic tree | Actual | Collector |
|---|---|---|
| Parent with 2 turns, fork with those 2 plus 1 new | 3 prompts, 6600 tokens | 5 prompts, 9900 tokens |
| Parent including one subagent's spend, plus the child session | 5500 tokens, 1 session | 6600 tokens, 2 sessions |

The fork case follows Grok's copy code directly. The subagent case is modelled on Grok's source, not observed on a real `~/.grok`.

**Impact:** inflated prompt, session, per-day and per-model counts, which also carry into synced snapshots.

**Suggested change:** skip session directories whose `summary.json` has a `session_kind` starting with `subagent` (#10400 does this; #12352 filters subagent-tagged events instead), and drop inherited fork turns, for example by reading `parent_session_id` and the fork point from `summary.json`, or by de-duplicating turns across files.

### Credit usage below 1 % is read as a fraction

Grok defines `creditUsagePercent` as "a percentage of the allowance (0.0 to 100.0)" (`xai-grok-shell/src/extensions/billing.rs:61`), and its TUI always treats it that way. `parse_billing` reuses a scale heuristic: it divides by 100 only when some value is at least 1 (lines 570 and 500).

| `creditUsagePercent` | Grok meaning | Panel shows |
|---|---|---|
| `0.4` | 0.4 % | 40 % |
| `0.95` (Build `0.6`) | 0.95 % | 95 %, bar alarm set |
| `1.0` | 1 % | 1 % |

**Impact:** every weekly period starts at zero, so a nearly unused pool can show as almost exhausted and raise the bar alarm early in the week.

Related gaps in the same parser:
- A payload without `creditUsagePercent` produces no rows, so when no cached window is still open (as right after a weekly reset) the section reports "Grok limits unavailable". The CLI treats a missing value as 0 %. Whether the live endpoint omits the field at zero usage is not confirmed.
- The deprecated `monthlyLimit`/`used` shape also produces no rows, while the CLI derives a percentage from it. The limits test's "legacy" case includes `creditUsagePercent: 25`, so it does not exercise that shape.

**Suggested change:** always divide `creditUsagePercent` and `usagePercent` by 100, and treat a missing `creditUsagePercent` as 0 when `currentPeriod` is present. An always-divide variant still passes the PR's tests.

### Cache-write tokens are counted twice

Grok's `prompt_tokens` includes cache reads and cache writes (`xai-grok-sampling-types/src/conversation.rs:772-787`), and the Codex collector subtracts both. `split_tokens` (line 144) subtracts only cache reads, then adds cache writes as their own bucket. A synthetic turn totals 130 tokens where Grok's own total is 110.

**Impact:** inflated token totals for Grok sessions on Anthropic Messages backends, the only backends that report cache writes.

**Suggested change:** subtract cache writes as well as cache reads from `inputTokens` in `split_tokens`. The scanner test currently expects the double-counted value (214 rather than 210), so its expected numbers need updating along with the fix.

### Other notes

**Open question, Build meter spelling:** the collector matches only `"product": "GrokBuild"` (line 545 onward). Grok's only public fixture for this shape uses `PRODUCT_GROK_BUILD` (`billing.rs:568-570`) and notes the CLI does not read `productUsage` yet. In that fixture the Build figure (61.2) is higher than the pool (42.5), which does not fit a "share of the weekly pool" meter; shown as a limit, such a value can become the headline and set the alarm. A redacted real response would settle both points; accepting both spellings is a cheap hardening.

**Smaller notes:**
- `CLIENT_VERSION = "1.0.41"` is sent as `x-grok-client-version`, which Grok's `agent/proxy_headers.rs` describes as required by the proxy's version gate. A raised minimum would make the billing probe fail while local stats continue.
- The PR description still says the tab has no limits meter and lists only the scanner test; the second commit adds the billing probe, token refresh and limits test.
- `manual/17-ai.md` says Grok's paid plans "share one weekly credit pool". Grok's source treats unified billing as a per-user setting with weekly or monthly periods, and the collector itself labels monthly periods.
- `AUTH_HELP` ("sign in to start recording usage") is shown while local usage is already being recorded; sign-in only gates the limits.

### Related open PRs

- #6485, #12352 and #10400 each add `bin/omarchy-agent-usage-grok` and Grok icons at the same paths, so they conflict with this PR and only one can land. #6485 and #10400 fetch billing through the Grok CLI, #12352 and #10400 skip subagent sessions, and #10400 always divides `creditUsagePercent` by 100.
- #12265 moves the Claude and Codex usage caches to owner-only permissions. This collector sets its caches to 0644 and its tests assert that mode, so it would be inconsistent with the other collectors if #12265 lands.
- #9733 and #7297 rename the Grok agent to "Grok Build" in docs and menus, which affects naming consistency with `AGENT_NAME = "Grok"`.

**Verified:** Grok's nanosecond RFC 3339 timestamps are attributed to the right local day, malformed `usage.json` files are skipped, `GROK_HOME` is honoured, cache writes are atomic under concurrent writers, the unwritable-cache fallback works, no token appears in stdout, stderr or the caches, and without `auth.json` the collector makes no network request (with no sessions either, the tab stays hidden). Scan cost was about 0.45 s per 1000 sessions of 20 turns on a warm in-memory filesystem, a lower bound.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR head `72221e9a` against the Omarchy collectors, update command and agents panel QML, and the Grok CLI's public Rust source. The PR tests, existing agent-usage tests, the real `omarchy-agent-usage-update`, mutants and behavioural probes ran in an isolated sandbox with no network and synthetic `~/.grok` data and fake tokens. No xAI endpoint or real account was used, so live IdP rotation, token lifetime and the live billing response shape are untested. The panel was not rendered on a desktop.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
